🔊 Pezeshkian stresses resilience and regional cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said his administration is expanding regional cooperation, strengthening domestic infrastructure, and accelerating railway development to counter the impact of sanctions while maintaining economic stability and public services.

Speaking about Iran's regional policy, President Pezeshkian said closer ties with neighboring countries have helped expand trade despite financial restrictions. He noted that while banking limitations have made money transfers difficult, barter trade has become one of the alternatives for maintaining commercial exchanges.
​
In an interview with the IRIB at the beginning of the third year of his tenure, President Pezeshkian also praised neighboring countries for their security cooperation, saying they prevented attempts by hostile groups to enter Iran from border regions and create unrest during recent periods of conflict and tension. He described this cooperation as an important achievement made possible through regional coordination and national unity.
​
President Pezeshkian said building unity and cooperation both with neighboring countries and within Iran was neither easy nor accidental, but had played a crucial role in frustrating plans aimed at destabilizing the country. He credited the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution with providing strong support for the government and its policies during critical periods, saying his guidance and backing helped the administration overcome major challenges.
​
Whenever officials faced difficulties, they turned to the martyred Leader, and he supported them with all his strength, Pezeshkian said. He added that Iran's resilience was the result of those policies, strategic direction, and guidance, and said the current Leader continues to encourage national unity and cohesion, helping the country address its challenges.
​
Addressing the impact of sanctions, President Pezeshkian said that restrictions on oil exports have reduced Iran's foreign currency earnings but stressed that the government is working with economists, academics, business professionals, chambers of commerce, and industry representatives to minimize economic challenges.
​
The officials have not solved every problem, but they are working together to reduce the impact of challenges, he said, adding that many foreign observers had expected Iran's economy to collapse under mounting pressure but had been surprised by its resilience.
​
The president said public cooperation has also played a key role in managing energy demand. He noted that nearly 7,000 megawatts of solar power capacity has already been added to the national grid, with further expansion underway. Despite damage to power plants and disruptions affecting approximately 230 million cubic meters of daily gas production, Iran has largely avoided widespread electricity outages, he said, adding that the government aims to prevent power cuts for industries and ensure stable energy supplies during the coming winter.
​
President Pezeshkian emphasized that expanding rail transportation remains one of his administration's top infrastructure priorities. He said the more than 600-kilometer Chabahar–Zahedan railway is scheduled to open during Government Week (August 23-29) despite delays caused by attacks on steel production facilities. The line will eventually connect to Sarakhs, strengthening Iran's national transport corridor.
​
He also announced that land acquisition for the Rasht–Astara railway has been completed and that construction is expected to proceed with Russian participation. In ad . . .

Crypto Idea

Long-Term investing strategy

When the crypto market is falling, buying feels scary. When it's going up, it feels like you've already missed your chance.

As a result, most people either buy based on emotion or keep waiting for the perfect entry point — and end up doing nothing at all.

But there's a simple way to avoid this problem: invest a fixed amount of money at regular intervals.

This strategy is called DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging).

You simply choose the asset, the amount you want to invest, and how often you want to buy.

For example:
$50 worth of Bitcoin every week.

When Bitcoin is cheaper, your $50 buys more. When it's more expensive, it buys less. Over time, your average purchase price naturally evens out, and over the course of a few years, it often ends up being better than the average market participant's.

Bybit even has a built-in Auto-Invest bot designed specifically for this strategy. You set it up once — choose your currency, the coin, the investment amount, and the schedule.

After that, your purchases happen automatically, whether it's every day or once a month. The key is to choose a coin you genuinely believe in for the long term.

📌 Market vs Limit Orders: Why “Buy Now” Can Be the Worst Choice

Main Points
⏺ Market orders give speed, but you give up price control
⏺ Limit orders give price control, but execution isn’t guaranteed
⏺ This post explains how order type changes slippage and risk

1️⃣ Market — you take liquidity immediately and pay spread + slippage.
2️⃣ Limit — you set a price and wait; if the market never reaches it, you don’t get filled.
3️⃣ Volatility Amplifies Pain — during fast moves, market fills can be far worse than expected.
4️⃣ DEX Parallel — high slippage settings basically turn a swap into “market at any price,” enabling bad execution.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — use limits when price matters more than speed, and don’t chase fills at any cost.

Final Thoughts

Speed isn’t always alpha. Sometimes real risk management is patience and price control.

Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) by hand ✍️ ~ 9 steps walkthrough below

The Gen in GenAI came from this landmark paper by Ian Goodfellow et al., 12 years ago.

The paper showed that a neural network can not only classify but also turn upside down to generate realistic looking images.

The secret? We pit two of them against each other: a Generator turns noise into fake data, and a Discriminator learns to tell fake from real, pushing the Generator to keep doing better.

One runs upside down, the other right way up.

I drew and calculated one entirely by hand.

Goal: generate realistic 4D data out of 2D noise, filling in every cell yourself.

= 1. Given =

Four noise vectors in 2D, and four real data vectors in 4D.

= 2. Generator, first layer =

Let us multiply the noise by weights and biases to get new features.

= 3. ReLU =

We apply the activation, and -1 and -2 are crossed out and set to 0.

= 4. Generator, second layer =

Let us multiply again. ReLU applies here too, but every value is already positive, so nothing changes. What comes out is the fake data F, made by a two-layer generator out of nothing but noise.

= 5. Discriminator, first layer =

We feed it both, the four fakes and the four real vectors, through the same weights. It never learns which is which from the layout, only from the numbers.

= 6. Discriminator, second layer =

Let us reduce each data vector to a single feature Z. Eight vectors in, eight numbers out.

= 7. Sigmoid =

We turn each Z into a probability Y. A 1 means the discriminator is certain the data is real, a 0 means certain it is fake.

= 8. Training the Discriminator =

Let us take the gradients as Y minus YD, where YD is what the discriminator should have said: 0 for the four fakes, 1 for the four real. Why so simple? Because pairing sigmoid with binary cross entropy loss makes the math collapse to exactly this subtraction. Its loss uses both halves of the page.

= 9. Training the Generator =

We do it again, as Y minus YG, and YG is [1, 1, 1, 1]: the generator wants the discriminator to call every fake real. Same predictions, different target, opposite goal. Its loss uses only the fakes.

The outputs:
Fake data F = [1, 2, 3, 1], [1, 1, 2, 1], [2, 2, 4, 2], [1, 0, 1, 1]
Predictions on fakes = [.7, .5, .9, .3]
